title: General Principles of Extraction of Metals
notes: **Concentration:** removing gangue to increase metal content. Methods: gravity separation, magnetic separation, froth flotation, leaching.
**Calcination:** heating ore in absence of air to remove volatile impurities and moisture. Carbonate ores decompose: $CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2$.
**Roasting:** heating ore in excess air to convert sulphide ores to oxides: $2ZnS + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2ZnO + 2SO_2$.
**Smelting:** reducing the oxide ore with carbon at high temperature: $ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO$.
**Carbon reduction:** used for metals less reactive than carbon. Carbon acts as reducing agent because it has higher affinity for oxygen.
**Thermite:** highly exothermic reaction of metal oxide with aluminium powder: $Fe_2O_3 + 2Al \rightarrow 2Fe + Al_2O_3 + \text{heat}$. Used for welding railway tracks.
**Electrochemical reduction:** used for very reactive metals like Na, K, Al. Electrolysis of molten salts: $2NaCl \rightarrow 2Na + Cl_2$.
